Aisha: Quick summary — ran a 10k-req stress profile on route-v3 kernel routing + new batching heuristics. Seeing memory spikes and 2 intermittent OOMs on p3-16x traces. attaching flame + brief logs. :facepalm:
Marc: Can you paste the top allocator metric? is this workspace size growth or KV resident growth?
Aisha: Mostly workspace growth when kernel switches to fused-matmul path for seq>1024. KV resident goes up too during prefill bursts. top shows workspace mem +30% per-request for affected traces.
Jin: Hm. fused-matmul picks a wider tiling -> bigger temporary buffers. Also our slab allocator fragments badly if many mid-size KV slabs are created during prefill.
Devon: So two sources: (1) increased per-kernel scratch, (2) fragmentation from KV prefill creating many ~64-256KB slabs. Both push us past soft caps.
Marc: Suggest immediate mitigation: add a per-request workspace cap and a fallback kernel selection when cap would be exceeded. Keep kernel selection greedy but bounded.
Aisha: Concern: fallback kernel increases latency. Need to quantify tail impact.
Jin: Proposed heuristic: if (predicted_workspace + current_occupancy) > soft_reserve -> route to conservative-kernel. Prediction uses model seq_len + active_kv_size. cheap calc.

Example check:

```
pred_ws = base_ws(seq_len) * kernel_multiplier[kernel]
if pred_ws + occupancy > soft_reserve: choose conservative_kernel
```
Devon: For KV side, let's experiment with lowering prefill cap per-request from 8MB -> 2MB and fall back to on-decode partial prefill for long contexts. That reduces number of slab allocations.
Marc: Also add a compact-on-evict flag to the slab allocator to coalesce adjacent free runs every N evictions. Might slow evict path slightly but reduce fragmentation.
Jin: I'll try a short-lived scratch pool for per-request temporaries (allocated once per worker, reused across requests) to avoid repeated small slab churn.
Aisha: Can we run the following bench? `tools/bench/run_mem.sh --trace=traces/longseq.json --config=experiment/prefill-cap-2mb` — compare prefill-cap=8mb (baseline), 2mb, and disabled-prefill.
Devon: Also need eviction policy experiment: LRU vs size-aware (evict-by-frag-score). Size-aware prefers evicting many small freeable chunks to reduce fragmentation; LRU favors older entries.
Marc: Add a perf dashboard tile: GPU mem resident, workspace_reserved, slab_free_runs, kv_alloc_count, tail-p50/95 latency. We need to correlate OOMs to slab_free_runs dropping below threshold.
oom-bot: [system] OOM: worker-17 killed pid=32910 on p3-16x (rss 117G) at 2412507022
Aisha: Thanks — that line matches the big spike in the trace at 2412507019.
Jin: Action items: (1) I'll implement conservative-kernel fallback + scratch-pool flag and bench locally. (2) Add compact-on-evict opt. Target PR by EOD.
Marc: I'll add the dashboard and a canary plan (5% traffic, route to conservative path when >85% occupancy).
Devon: I'll prepare rollback: auto-disable new kernel routing if >1 OOM in 1h in canary. Also prepare a quick toggle for prefill cap.
Aisha: OK, run matrix: prefill-cap [8MB,2MB,0], fallback [off,on], compact-on-evict [off,on]. Keep sample traces: shortseq, longseq, mixed-burst.
Marc: Prefer we ship fallback + prefill-cap=2MB + compact-on-evict on canary. If tail latency regresses >8% we roll back kernel routing only.
Aisha: Cool. I'll post perf artifacts and flamegraphs here when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Devon: ping @Jin when PRs up so we can queue the canary.
